title: Exclude 6,105 two-packet BIT deletions with recoded ingress senders
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

For every pair of the 111 specified terminal packets, the two targets are outside the pooled strict-preclock source span of every surviving ingress to both banks. This permits arbitrary recoding at those ingresses and free terminal decoding with the earlier senders fixed. The companion proves that with ingress equations fixed, a single earlier additive pulse also fails all 6,105 pairs because their two required correction sets are disjoint. The complete conditional κ is unchanged.

## Task and overlap

This is a refined follow-up to [#7852](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7852) at `41beda1d6435760dc99e38bd7e65f36798aad212`, on main `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`. The pinned word is [#7830](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7830) at `87fbf4f7b35b0f18ab12b5767775a9a424cf0b15`. [#7978](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7978) at `dd529bbb031cf87b424d43841a88a009773fa24b` and [#7985](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7985) at `251e15df3e0c058a843e7cb13f5882179a4e3afc` supply the fixed-sender and terminal-redecoding context. The two new recoding models retain different fixed equations; each archive specifies its own class.

## Validation

In separate empty Python 3.12 extractions of each archive run `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS`, `python3 -IB screen.py --verify` and `python3 -IB raw_verify.py --verify`. The independent tape checks reproduced 35,640 leave-one-out cuts, 12,210 forbidden-restoration controls and the companion’s literal 680-row pulse mutation.

## Open next questions

Test two earlier changing senders or a new paid route, then replay both complete native orientations, signed ranks and the physical and finite outer application for a surviving construction.
